name: Freeport-McMoRan
thesis: Freeport is the largest publicly traded copper producer and a leveraged, low-cost play on a structural copper deficit, with a gold/moly byproduct stream that subsidizes unit costs. FY2025 delivered $25.9B revenue, $5.6B operating cash flow and ~$9.9B adjusted EBITDA at a net cash cost of just $1.65/lb, even after the Sept 8, 2025 Grasberg mud rush (7 fatalities) cut FY copper ~10%. The investment case is volume re-rating plus price: Grasberg Block Cave (~70% of PTFI's forecast copper/gold through 2029) began a phased restart in March 2026, with consolidated Grasberg copper guided to recover from ~1.0Bn lbs in 2025-26 to 1.5Bn (2027) and 1.7Bn (2028). Layered on top is organic US growth that needs no new orebody: 'Freeport leaching' targets 300-400 Mlbs/yr by 2026-27 ramping toward 800 Mlbs by ~2030 from ~42Bn lbs of stockpiled copper, plus Bagdad (+200-250 Mlbs), Lone Star (+300-400 Mlbs) and El Abra (+700 Mlbs). At $6.00/lb copper, management guides ~$8.7B 2026 operating cash flow. Copper itself sits near a record ~$6/lb against a forecast 2026 deficit of 330k-600k tonnes (JPM/Morgan Stanley) as grid, EV and AI-datacenter demand collide with falling global ore grades. What's PRICED IN: at ~$61/share, ~$92-97B market cap and ~11.8x EV/EBITDA (vs a ~7.9x 10-yr median) on already-cut 2026 EPS, the stock already capitalizes record copper, a clean Grasberg ramp, and the Manyar smelter at full run-rate. Margin of safety is thin if copper mean-reverts toward $4 (each $0.10/lb move is ~$390M of EBITDA), if the GBC restart slips, or if Indonesia (51%+ state-controlled via MIND ID) tightens export, royalty or divestment terms. This is a cyclical, single-commodity, capex-heavy miner priced for the bull case to compound, not merely hold.
key_driver: Realized copper price times salable volumes (Grasberg ramp + leaching/brownfield) minus net unit cash cost — at ~$6/lb copper FCX guides ~$8.7B operating cash flow, but the same EBITDA roughly halves at $4 copper, so the thesis lives or dies on price x volume staying ahead of costs.

nuance.bear_case: FCX is a price-taker on a single cyclical commodity trading near record highs (~$6/lb COMEX in mid-2026, above Goldman's ~$5.00/lb fair value), with brutal two-way operating leverage: each $0.10/lb copper move = ~$390M EBITDA and ~$300M operating cash flow. Earnings are discounting peak-cycle pricing at a 40x+ trailing P/E. The flagship Grasberg (51%+ Indonesian state-controlled via MIND ID) suffered a fatal Sept-2025 mud rush (~800kt wet material, 7 dead/missing, force majeure) that gutted Q4'25 sales to 'insignificant' and forced 2026 copper guidance down to ~3.1B lb (from ~3.4B) and gold to ~650koz (from ~800koz), with bottlenecks lingering toward 2027. Net unit cash cost guidance was hiked to ~$1.95/lb from $1.75 on lower volumes and diesel inflation. Capex is climbing to $4.3-4.5B in 2026 (Bagdad, Kucing Liar, the Manyar smelter) just as FCF compressed sharply in 2025. Indonesia controls the IUPK extension, divestment, and export licensing — structural, non-diversifiable risk.
nuance.adversarial_take: Bulls extrapolate three things they shouldn't: (1) that copper stays at/above record levels indefinitely — yet surplus forecasts and softening Chinese demand argue otherwise; (2) that Grasberg ramps flawlessly back to plan after a fatal cave collapse that already cost a quarter of output and pushed full recovery to 2027; (3) that ~40x trailing earnings is 'cheap' because it's on depressed 2026 EPS. That's the classic miner value trap — a low multiple on peak earnings is expensive, a high multiple on trough earnings only works if the cycle re-accelerates AND execution is perfect. You're paying a premium (EV/EBITDA ~11.8x vs ~7.9x 10-yr median) for a leveraged bet on copper price AND Indonesian goodwill AND operational redemption. Right posture: Watch, don't chase; the asymmetric entry is a copper pullback toward fair value with the Grasberg ramp de-risked, not paying up for all three at once.
nuance.stress_test: If copper falls to ~$4.00/lb (a plausible recession/surplus print, ~$2/lb below spot) AND Grasberg's ramp slips again or the export licence/IUPK extension stalls: the price move alone strips ~$7-8B of annualized EBITDA (~$2/lb x ~$390M per $0.10), on top of lost copper volume. Operating cash flow (~$5.6B in 2025) could halve or worse while $4.3-4.5B capex is largely committed, flipping FCF deeply negative and pushing net debt past the $3-4B target. The performance-based variable dividend (~$0.075/qtr) gets cut first, and a 40x peak P/E re-rates toward trough multiples — a double hit of falling E and falling multiple.

thesis_breakers_qualitative: Copper sustainably below ~$4.00/lb on a global/China demand recession or a widening forecast surplus, collapsing EBITDA via the ~$390M-per-$0.10 lever.
Net unit cash cost printing above ~$2.50/lb on diesel/labor/grade decline as the Grasberg underground transition lowers ore grades.
Grasberg ramp slipping past mid-2027, a second mud-rush/wet-muck or fatality event, or another force majeure cutting 2027 copper (planned ~1.5B lb) / gold guidance.
Indonesia withholding or delaying the copper-concentrate export licence, or IUPK extension / additional-divestment terms turning materially adverse to FCX economics.
Capex overruns at the Manyar smelter, Bagdad (~$3.5B) or Kucing Liar pushing 2026-27 capex above ~$4.5B and keeping FCF near/below zero.
The performance-based variable dividend being cut/suspended to defend the $3-4B net-debt target as the cycle turns.
Net debt breaching ~$4B (incl. PTFI smelter project debt) in a down-cycle, triggering balance-sheet/return-of-capital retrenchment.

break_rules.narrative: Revenue declining YoY for 2 consecutive quarters — outright top-line contraction.
GAAP operating margin negative for 2 consecutive quarters — operating loss.
FCF margin below 5% for 2 consecutive Qs — cash conversion broken. (Universal floor; per-ticker rules below are stricter.)

business_model_rules.narrative: As a single-commodity copper miner with price-takers' economics, two straight quarters of revenue down >15% YoY almost always signals a copper-price downcycle (not a share-loss problem); because EBITDA and free cash flow are highly price-elastic, this is the earliest hard read that the leveraged bull thesis is being tested.

Mining operating margin is the spread between realized copper (plus gold/moly credits) and largely fixed mine costs; sustained operating margin below 15% means the low-cost-producer advantage has been overwhelmed by falling copper or cost inflation, eroding the thesis's core source of cash generation.

FCX is capex-heavy (Grasberg underground, smelter, leaching, brownfields); capex consuming >30% of revenue for two quarters means growth spend is outrunning a shrinking revenue base, threatening free cash flow, the variable dividend and the net-debt band — the discipline that distinguishes a value-creating miner from a value-destroyer through the cycle.

The bull case rests on copper cash flow funding both growth and shareholder returns; two consecutive quarters of negative FCF margin means the company is burning cash to mine at prevailing prices, forcing debt accumulation toward/above the $4B ceiling and shutting off the performance-based payout that anchors total return.
